news_analysis.headline_hook: Hero Motors +20%: Why the math says your upside is capped at 4.2%.
news_analysis.breaking_event_summary: Hero Motors shares surged 20% in a single session to hit ₹141.85 on September 25, taking its total post-IPO gain to nearly 69% over the ₹84 issue price despite early listing weakness.
news_analysis.retail_illusion: Retail traders believe the 20% upper-circuit style rally confirms strong fundamental discovery, triggering FOMO buying at the top under the belief of guaranteed momentum.
news_analysis.institutional_reality: A rapid 69% vertical spike from ₹84 to ₹141.85 post-weak listing often reflects low float liquidity squeezes and institutional exit engineering, leaving late retail buyers holding overvalued stock right before stabilization and multiple compression.
news_analysis.actionable_retail_rule: Never chase vertical 20% rallies on newly listed IPOs without price stabilization and proven quarterly earnings support.

slides.title: The Retail vs Institutional Reality Check

comparison_data.myth: Retail belief: A 20% circuit confirms fundamental strength and guaranteed momentum.
comparison_data.reality: Institutional truth: A 69% vertical spike from ₹84 to ₹141.85 often signals a low-float liquidity squeeze used for institutional exit engineering.

stat_data.label: Estimated retail capital erosion per high-volume exit
stat_data.context: When retail chases a 20% vertical rally, they absorb the liquidity provided by institutional sellers. This mathematical friction occurs as the stock hits premium valuation caps, leading to inevitable multiple compression.

slides.title: The Liquidity Trap Mechanism
flowchart_data: 3. Institutional players offload positions into the retail buying frenzy.

slides.title: How Capital is Quietly Extracted
slides.card_text: By buying at the peak of a 20% surge, you are purchasing at a premium valuation that lacks quarterly earnings support. As the stock stabilizes, the price reverts to the mean, effectively transferring your capital to early institutional investors who exited at the top.

slides.title: The Non-Negotiable Institutional Rule
slides.card_text: Never chase vertical 20% rallies on newly listed IPOs. Institutional pros wait for price stabilization and proven quarterly earnings support before entering. If the chart looks like a vertical line, the risk-to-reward ratio is mathematically broken.
